title: HBMex: An Attachment for Nonbursting Accelerators to Enhance HBM Performance
problem: Applications with irregular, nonbursting memory access patterns (SpMV, graph analytics) cannot effectively utilize HBM's high bandwidth, and the HBM interconnect may stall requests under certain conditions.
motivation: Modern FPGAs offer substantial bandwidth through HBM, but important irregular-access workloads remain underutilized due to poor memory access characteristics.
method: HBMex is a configurable module positioned between the accelerator and HBM that distributes memory requests across multiple HBM interfaces to improve parallelism. It mitigates interconnect stalls by intelligently routing requests to balance load and exploit available bandwidth across interfaces.
key_novelty: A specialized attached module that addresses HBM interconnect bottlenecks by distributing irregular memory requests across multiple interfaces.
contributions: HBMex module designed to enhance HBM throughput for non-bursting accelerators
Request distribution technique across multiple HBM interfaces to reduce interconnect stalls
37% throughput improvement on real-world SpMV workloads versus vendor solutions
Open-source configurable RTL generator for easy integration
limitations: Paper limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: HBM throughput optimization for irregular memory access patterns
